chapter: Zach White, Cotton Pickers and Cab Calloway
title: Leaving the Cotton Pickers: the fight over Billy Borne's clarinet
summary: When he gave notice, the Cotton Pickers refused his pay; he took Billy Borne's clarinet and a brawl followed. Cab lent him $100, and Barefield impressed him by writing arrangements overnight.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Oh, I know what. Your notice.
So I went back and gave the Cotton
Pickers my notice that I was going with Cab Calloway and they all got mad. And I was using Billy Borne's clarinet and so they --
So I said -- in fact, he was conducting for McKinney, too, because McKinney was a drummer but he didn't play in the band.

So anyway they wouldn't pay me my salary. I just told -- I took the clarinet, Billy Borne's clarinet. Then that started a fight. There was a free-for-all on the bandstand and everybody jumped on me but Prince and Roy Eldridge. And I was just BEATING guys all over the bandstand. So we fought all the way down to the hotel.
How much of a distance is that?

Oh, maybe ten or fifteen blocks. Well, we were fighting in the cars, used to ride in cars and things. So finally, they didn't pay me anyway and I ended up with a black eye. And I went back to the theater the next day and Cab said, what happened? And I told him and he said, 'well, how much money do you need?' And I said, 'well, I just need some money to get my laundry out, pay my rent and all that.' He said, 'here's $100.00, will that do it?' So I -- you know, we were only getting $30.00 a week so $100.00 was

So anyway, we -- I had told Cab I wrote and he gave me a couple of things to write and make some arrangements on, "Little Town Gal" and "Harlem Hospitality." So I went home that night and brought the arrangements back the next day which he thought was fantastic, you know. Because at that time I had learned how to write, just sit down and write.

So the last day he put me on the stage with the band and they were wearing those brown tails. So they put a double breasted coat on me and pinned it back so it'd look, while I'm sitting -- so then he wanted to know what I'd do about parts. Oh, I'd write my own parts.
